report.summary: Chunk 4 of 7 of docrefs.py: contains helper functions _module_file, _collect_names, _parse_cache, and resolve_reference. No new claims or symbols beyond what is defined.

handoff.purpose: Define helper functions for resolving references: file path resolution, AST name collection, cache parsing, and reference resolution.

symbols.name: _module_file
symbols.note: Returns the Path to a module file given root and parts; checks .py file and __init__.py, then uses suffix index if provided.

symbols.name: _collect_names
symbols.note: Collects top-level names, class members, and dynamic flag from AST body; walks into if/try bodies.

symbols.name: _parse_cache
symbols.note: Reads a module file, parses it, caches the result; returns names, classes, dynamic, error string.

symbols.name: resolve_reference
symbols.note: Decides whether a Reference exists; never raises; returns Reference with state and why.

claims.text: Top-level names, class members, and whether the namespace is DYNAMIC. Walks into module-level ``if``/``try`` bodies, because a conditional or guarded import is a normal way to define a public name and missing it would manufacture a false "this symbol does not exist".
claims.why: The code iterates over ast.stmt nodes and explicitly handles If and Try by recursing into their bodies, orelse, finalbody, and handlers.

claims.text: Decide whether ``ref`` names code that exists. Never raises.
claims.why: The function signature and implementation (no try/except visible) indicate it never raises; the docstring states it.

claims.text: The precondition for judging AT ALL is that the module resolves. A reference whose module is absent is ``skipped`` -- see the module docstring on why that is the entire false-positive filter.
claims.why: The module docstring is not in this chunk; the logic for skipping absent modules is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: known non-module dotted name; a coincidental module basename must not turn it into an autonomous edit target
claims.where: resolve_reference docstring (via code comment in the function)
claims.why: _NON_MODULE_DOTTED_NAMES is not defined in this chunk; the check is present but the set's contents are not visible.

observations.what: Function _module_file accepts optional suffixes parameter but the method of using it is not fully visible; it checks if len(hits)==1.
resolve_reference uses cache.get('__suffixes__') and sets it if missing, but the cache dict is passed in; the function also uses _NON_MODULE_DOTTED_NAMES which is not defined in this chunk.
